title: Edmund and the Garden
premise: Felix Almeida, the last oath-bound swordspeaker, has spent her whole life in the valley where magic cannot follow — a sanctuary that is also a cage, and a bargain her ancestors made to survive. When a dying stranger presses a map into her hands and dies speaking her name, Felix learns her family's survival was purchased with a soul sold to the court beneath the mountain: her own mother's. Guided by Edmund, a garden-keeper who is more than he seems, she descends into the winter court to steal the soul back before the long winter finishes falling and seals the valley forever. She succeeds only by surrendering her oath and her magic, returning soulless of power but whole of heart, and choosing to stay in the valley not because she must, but because it is hers.
about_author: Xanthe Reyes is a former botanist who traded greenhouses for manuscripts after a decade cataloguing alpine flora in remote valleys. Her fiction braids folklore, grief, and the stubbornness of living things.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. We meet the valley where magic cannot follow: Felix tends graves, drills sword-forms no enemy will ever come for, and chafes at an oath she barely understands. A stranger staggers out of the pass, frostbitten and wrong. Emotional beat: restless duty curdling into dread.

chapters.title: A Map Pressed Into Unwilling Hands
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The dying stranger grips Felix's wrist, calls her by a name no one uses, and presses a bloodstained map into her hands with words about 'the debt' and 'the court beneath.' He dies as the first snow falls weeks early. Emotional beat: guilt and unwanted inheritance.

chapters.title: What the Elders Will Not Say
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix confronts the valley elders; they admit fragments — the Founding Bargain, a soul given as surety, the long winter as collection notice. They forbid her to leave. That night she burns nothing and packs everything. Emotional beat: betrayal by protection.

chapters.title: Edmund of the Garden
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, introducing Edmund. At the valley's edge stands an impossible garden, green in the snow, kept by Edmund, a gentle man who remembers every plant and no years. He claims he was left behind too. He offers to guide her over the pass. Emotional beat: wary kinship between two leftovers.

chapters.title: The Pass of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Alternating POV begins. Crossing the mountains, Felix discovers her swordspeech — inert in the valley — wakes outside it, singing through her blade. Edmund watches her wonder with something like sorrow. They survive an avalanche by his uncanny knowledge of growing things. Emotional beat: intoxicating first taste of self.

chapters.title: The Road Remembers
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. On the road, Edmund recalls a woman who once walked this way carrying a sleeping child — Felix's mother, fleeing down-mountain, not up. He keeps this to himself. Bandits test Felix; her speech flares wild and frightening. Emotional beat: the past moving beneath the present like roots.

chapters.title: The Town of Sold Names
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. In a border town where people pawn memories to a broker, Felix trades a happy memory for passage information and feels the hole it leaves. She learns others have gone beneath the mountain and not returned. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal and small.

chapters.title: Winter Finishes Falling
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The long winter arrives early and hard, sealing passes and shortening days unnaturally. Refugees crowd the roads; some are already gray-eyed and quiet, half-claimed. Edmund realizes the court is harvesting early. Emotional beat: urgency sharpening into fear.

chapters.title: The Door Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Following the map to a door carved with her family crest, Felix speaks it open with words from her oath — the oath was always a key. Inside, warmth like a held breath. Edmund hesitates at the threshold. Emotional beat: crossing from quest into commitment.

chapters.title: The Court of Quiet Hours
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The subterranean court: beautiful, slow, lit by stored summers. Its steward greets Felix as 'the collateral's daughter' and offers hospitality that is also custody. She sees shelves of bottled souls, each labeled with a name. Emotional beat: awe laced with horror.

chapters.title: A Soul on a Shelf
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix finds her mother's soul-bottle, still warm, still humming a lullaby. The steward explains the bargain: the valley's safety was bought with one soul per generation, renewable if unclaimed. Claiming it voids everything. Emotional beat: love versus loyalty to the living.

chapters.title: Edmund's Confession
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund reveals he was the first keeper of the garden — and the first soul sold, given leave to tend the valley's edge instead of sitting on a shelf. His gentleness is what remains when a court files away your rage. He begs her to weigh what theft will cost. Emotional beat: pity transforming into resolve.

chapters.title: Terms of Hospitality
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Negotiation with the steward: Felix may attempt the Rite of Return — carry the soul up through the falling winter before the last snow seals the door — but if she fails, both souls are forfeit. She agrees. Edmund refuses to be left. Emotional beat: signing a contract with your fear.

chapters.title: Theft of a Small Warm Thing
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The heist: Felix uses her swordspeech to cut the bottle free while Edmund's borrowed court-etiquette buys them minutes. Alarms are not bells here but silences, spreading room by room. They run. Emotional beat: triumph immediately chased by consequence.

chapters.title: Flight Through Stored Summers
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Pursuit through the court's season-rooms — spring floods, summer fire, autumn wind — each testing them. Edmund burns decades of himself to hold a door open. Felix carries two souls now: her mother's and, unknowingly, pieces of his. Emotional beat: sacrifice as intimacy.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Closes
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. They reach the door as the final snow begins. Behind them the court; ahead, the climb. The steward offers one last trade: the mother's soul for Edmund's return. Felix refuses, and the door grinds shut behind them all — including, she realizes, their way home. Emotional beat: point of no return.

chapters.title: Climbing Against the Snow
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The ascent through the finished winter, souls fading, bodies failing. Edmund gives Felix the truth of her mother's flight and asks forgiveness for silence. Felix, furious and grieving, keeps climbing anyway, singing the oath backward to keep the soul warm. Emotional beat: anger burned down to its gold core.

chapters.title: The Garden at the Edge
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. They reach the valley edge; the garden is dead under the new winter. To cross the boundary where magic cannot follow, the soul must be carried by someone already inside — impossible — unless someone becomes part of the valley itself. Edmund chooses: he takes root, becoming the garden again, alive and bound. Emotional beat: grief transfigured into rootedness.

chapters.title: Return of the Borrowed Heart
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Inside the valley, Felix performs the Rite of Return at her mother's grave. The soul rises, spends one breath as a presence — a hand on her hair, a lullaby finished — and dissolves into the thawing ground. The valley's bargain breaks; the long winter stops at the ridge. Emotional beat: release, and the ache after.

chapters.title: What the Oath Was For
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Without the bargain, the valley must survive honestly: Felix teaches swordspeech to volunteers, real defense at last, and helps rebuild the broken garden around Edmund's roots. The elders yield their seats. Emotional beat: purpose replacing inheritance.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath Waits
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV (rooted, dreaming). Deep below, the steward catalogs the loss without anger — courts are patient — and sets a new ledger page bearing Felix's name. Above, spring comes late but comes. Emotional beat: quiet menace balanced against earned hope.

chapters.title: Edmund and the Garden
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, closing frame. One year on: the garden blooms again, fed by Edmund's rooted dreams, which speak to Felix in leaf-patterns and birdsong. She stays — not exiled, not bound, but belonging. She plants the stranger's unnamed grave beside the gate and finally signs her full name in the valley's book. Emotional beat: home chosen, not inherited.
